Which statements are correct for a jointly multivariate normal pair of blocks?
items.explanation: A, B and C are true; D is false because the conditional covariance does not depend on the observed value.
statements: A marginal block is multivariate normal.
The conditional covariance is constant in the observed conditioning value.
The conditional mean is always equal to μ₂.

B.why: For joint normal blocks, zero cross-covariance implies independence.

C.why: The covariance formula contains only population covariance blocks.

D.why: The conditional mean generally shifts with x₁.

Which statements correctly distinguish marginal and conditional distributions?
items.explanation: A, B and C are true; D is false because conditional covariance is not generally equal to the marginal covariance.
statements: The marginal covariance of X₂ is Σ₂₂.
The conditional mean generally depends on x₁.
The conditional covariance generally equals Σ₂₂.

A.why: The marginal law keeps the lower-right covariance block.

C.why: The observed conditioning value shifts the conditional mean.

D.why: The conditional covariance is generally smaller than Σ₂₂.

The adjustment term always has the dimension p×p.
